svg.title: Repository onboarding path
svg.desc: Six commands scaffold config, pin the lock, compile context, record debt, prepare a devcontainer, and verify governance.

g.text: the six vendor files · same as init
audit fails on gaps · ruleset, tooling, hooks
does not pass audit on its own
init reads AGENTS.md beside the manifest; without it, init writes no agent files.
createInitialManifest and initBaselineAndLockfile write the manifest, an unpinned placeholder lockfile and a zero-debt baseline.
initAgentContext runs the compile-context write: Git ignores .workingdir/evidence/, the text register is spliced into AGENTS.md, and the six vendor files and
persona copies are compiled and linted.
profile set pins placeholder lockfile digests from the reviewed Praetor source root.
devcontainer generate and audit require sha256 digests; pinning also materializes the catalog under .config/archetypes/.
compile-context runs the same write that init ran.
writeAgentSurfaces copies every .agents/agents persona into each client persona directory, then the caveman lint runs.
HISS scanner sweeps the codebase for existing infractions.
Initial legacy debt is recorded with --allow-increase and --reason="<why>" to permit non-zero count.
DevContainer configuration and reviewed source bundle companions are generated.
JSON configuration and exact source companions are prepared; build and startup remain separate checks.
Audit checks manifest, lockfile, agent context, debt baseline, and DevContainer.
The staged alternative does not pass the audit on its own: ruleset, gate tooling and hooks remain missing.
One adopt run writes what steps 1 to 5 write, and synthesizes AGENTS.md when it is missing.
The path continues at step 6. init would now refuse: .standards.yaml already exists.
With git add -A, praetorctl audit --offline exits 0: the quickstart passes audit on its own.
